subject: The pitch field charted as a conic atlas sheet, scale degrees as meridians and loudness as parallels, with the flock plotted over it as one asterism whose stars carry proper-motion vectors.
controls: cohere: the asterism's spread over the chart (uniform scale about the flock's centre, about 2x across the range): at 0 the stars span most of the sheet, at 100 they knot into a few neighbouring meridians.
speed: each star's proper-motion vector, the distance flown in one beat (shape: 6 px at 0.25 to 32 px at 4.00), with the strip's raised marks as the second cue.
scatter: outlying stars leave the asterism and its join lines drop (position, up to ~60 px off the group's centre), so stray notes land far from the cluster.
scale: how many meridians the sheet ruled (count: 11 for penta, 25 for chrom over two octaves), each labelled octave meridian staying put.
reference: opxy/reference/field-and-figure.jpg (field at low grey, one bright figure, activity strip under it)
risks: chrom rules 25 meridians across ~360 px, ~14 px apart at the bottom and closer near the top; fine for spacing but the field gets loud, so meridians may need to fade toward the top.
Stars are 3-5 px; at 1:1 the asterism is small against the chart and the brightest element only by a little. Bigger stars or a dimmer field in the frames pass.
The strip is near-dashboard; it earns its place only if it's the note response (raised marks on play) rather than a permanent meter.
Muted: needs its own cue (stars hollow, vectors hidden), not just dimmer greys.
